newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Political future of Australia's Hanson less certai.
newsitem.headline: Political future of Australia's Hanson less certai.

text.p: Australian race row politician Pauline Hanson's political future is in doubt after a radical proposal to redraw her electorate boundaries would increase the opposition Labor Party's chances of winning the seat.

Under the Australian Electoral Commission's draft redistribution of the boundaries in the state of Queensland, Hanson's seat of Oxley has gained some of Australia's strongest Labor voting territory, while losing its conservative areas.
The redistribution was necessary because of the addition of one extra seat in Queensland to account for population growth.
Objections to the draft can be lodged until August 25, after which the commission has 60 days to consider them. Still, the commission was not expected to make changes to the draft.
Hanson, an independent who won office at the last election in March 1996, stands on an anti-immigration platform and has criticised Aboriginal welfare.
She sparked a divisive race debate last September when she said Australia was in danger of being swamped by Asians.
The next Australian election is due to be held before May 1999.
